Describe how groups are composed of roles

Source: R/groups.R
describe_groups.Rd

A family, a household or a workplace is a group of rows, and each row has a role in it: reference person, partner, child. The composition of a group is how many of each role it has, and describe_groups() counts the groups with each composition: "1 reference + 1 partner + 2 child: 4,210", "1 child: 12". Like the transition table of describe_transitions() it is the diagnosis itself: the impossible groups show before any rule is written. Require a composition with ensure_counts().

Usage

describe_groups(data, group, role)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

group

Column(s) identifying the group (tidy-select), e.g. c(family, year).

role

The role column (one column), e.g. role.

Value

An object of class inshape_groups, printed as a summary. It is a list with group, role, the counts n_rows and n_groups, roles (the roles, as text) and compositions, a tibble with one column per role holding its count, composition (the same as text) and groups, most common first.

Details

The group is what the group columns say: a family id, or a family id and a year for families over time. A missing role is a role of its own, shown as NA.

See also

ensure_counts() to require a composition, ensure_references() for rows that point to each other.

Examples

families <- data.frame(
  family = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4),
  role   = c("reference", "partner", "child", "reference", "child",
             "child", "reference", "reference")
)
# family 3 has no reference person, family 4 has two
describe_groups(families, family, role)
#> ── Groups: family by role ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 8 rows, 4 groups, 3 roles
#> 
#> • Compositions: 4
#> 
#> Most common compositions:
#>     composition                       groups share
#>   1 1 child                                1 25.0%
#>   2 1 child + 1 partner + 1 reference      1 25.0%
#>   3 1 child + 1 reference                  1 25.0%
#>   4 2 reference                            1 25.0%
